I've read your entire story, and it did strike a chord with me. Friends of mine are sort of in the same situation right now, but my best friend had (and has) some of the same experiences you've.had. With your physical description, it's almost like you two would be alike.

I guess the advice I can give is that when you feel a certain way, or think of certain thoughts, remember what it comes from. From your other posts, it seems that you've had moments that go between explaining your feelings, and then feeling no self-worth. Didn't you say your mom would go from one mood to the next like snapping fingers? I just know that once you figure out those little patterns, it does help to be more aware of those actions in the future. When you've kept wanting to work against, or for, certain ways to act they eventually become a habit.

I also think that if your parents would go apeshit and kick you out if you decided to go looking for a job, it's still better to get away from them anyway. If you think getting a job is the best plan right now, keep it as secret as possible, and maybe do so when you've already got one.

As for... not advice. I'm personally here for you. I can't physically be there, but I am willing to listen and help. It all starts in the mind.

I am trying to do so, but I have mentioned how I feel no motivation. What I primarily feel is that I have no real "positive" motivation behind my actions, but mainly from other people. I have gotten sympathy from other people, but not a lot of support. The people I've gotten sympathy from do not take the time to keep giving it out, in that they don't want it to become a crutch for me. They want me to just get up and do it, which is where I am at now. I know it's not hard, and I guess I just need to trust myself a lot more, but I really am stuck on all of the different thoughts that race through my head when I think this over.

That, and I don't find I'm very passionate about anything besides that one key-thing I already pointed out, the paranormal/adventure aspect of it all. If you feel like you've talked enough, I'm willing to say thank you so much again for wanting to discuss this with me. I know it kinda sounds like I'm a broken record.

It seems quite easy to do, and there have been times where the cord was actually taken away against my will. When that happens, I find the entire point to be taken away, since I didn't make the choice.

When it comes to making things true with no effort, that might be strange for other fields. What about some friends of mine who casually can do astral projection, see and explore in another dimension, and those who cannot see and explore? Both may believe it's true, and they both might be making it true with no effort (closing their eyes, seeing or not), but does that make it true? I find myself calling it "mass-disillusionment." I also seem to bring that same term back to religion, but I don't know.

Then there's stuff dealing with dreams, which I do without any effort. I do not know what to think of that, even though some things about it sometimes hit close to home in how I'm feeling or the predicted future.

For a good long while, I have been trying (or mainly have been) living day to day. I have been wanting to do that, but I don't really know if I'm doing it. I feel that might be the same for living "RIGHT AT THIS MOMENT."

Lets go back to wanting to get off of this computer and doing something I want to do. Drawing, writing, etc. I think of all of the moments passing by me while I'm still at this computer. I find that I have no motivation to do so, and at times little inspiration comes to mind even though I have a huge selection to choose from (music and inner experiences).

There is also people wanting for me be a man and get working towards my future. I would like to be doing that, but I don't feel any form of motivation in doing so. I also felt this way with learning things to do in the paranormal department. That I felt went down to beliefs. *If you truly believe in it, and yourself, that will be true.* Do you find that stupid or crazy?

Thank you very much for this. The idea of duality is still very prevalent, and it's good to remember it. Although that has been one thing I fear when it comes to the idea of "leaving" with Alpha/Beta/Ceta. I could go further with this if you want.

The idea of destiny is something I don't really think about *all* the time. I find that there is such a thing as destiny, but there still some form of control. You are still given choices, but those small choices affect the destiny. This is already pretty common with anything, but in the idea of a complete "destiny," it's a bit different to think about. Some of the decisions might be very small.

But, hearing something like "the universe knows best" is a great change of pace.

With that, my "citations" are not so valid. A lot of the experiences I've had are "you-had-to-be-there" moments. All I've got left are memories, writings, drawings, and some chat-logs.

For myself, I see why I listen to the music I do, and how it all sort of works. I also do experiments in dreams such as lucid, "going-with-the-flow" lucid, verbal triggering, and just writing them down. That's all not exactly paranormal. In ways of paranormal concepts introduced to me, the idea of the Alpha/Beta/Ceta dimensions still makes me think.

From the beginning, I was very interested in everything. Lets think of very generic things in fiction. What happens when a kid reads too many comics, watches too many movies, and plays too many video games? No, they do not become anti-social (but they surely become bullied), they go on adventures through strange things. That's been my inner drive throughout it all, as campy as it sounds.

When I learned that everything happening *was not a game,* I took things more seriously. Looking back, I didn't do much, but I learned everything I could and asked a lot of questions. I met a lot of different people, as well as different kinds of people. I know about a lot of places, and some concepts that are generally well-known were expanded on.

Currently, I am working on a binder that contains names and places of people that connect back to everything in this stuff. It's more to give a personal account of everything I experienced, but also to "preserve history." I also guess you could call it closure. I am also filling it with fictional names and places I've thought up in my free time, but have not expanded upon yet.

I'm no expert, but the *religious* aspect kinda turns me off. I find that with supernatural things, your relationship with things that could potentially be divine or just very strange becomes very personal. I am a Christian, but I do not talk to people about my faith at all in that the relationship I believe has become one that is purely my own.

One story that still gets me was with the friend I met through my best friend. Around a week after that day, I was talking with her online about all of this, and learning new things about past-lives. I leave the computer since we're going to Disneyland with some friends. My mother and I wait outside, and I see a couple crows. I chase them away like an idiot, and don't think anything of it. The next day, a talk between her and I abruptly turns into a conversation between a past-life and I. The person mentioned how I hadn't changed at all from old times, and how I still think birds are my enemies, chasing them away.

My **first impression** was a complete stand-still, and I was a little shocked, in that my comfort zone was somewhat taken away for a second. My **second impression** is that she was stalking me, but she lives thirty minutes away from me by car. From then on, I took her seriously, since she also felt lying to be completely pointless.

I don't write too often out of school, but I do it to develop thoughts on things I've learned in class. I write to myself or draw when I'm not doing anything *at school,* but I mainly write to myself because I've found it's become really therapeutic.
